subject: Observability kickstart: dashboards, tracing hooks & escalation wiring
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie@brightbridge.ai>, ops@brightbridge.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Apr 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Observability kickstart: dashboards, tracing hooks & escalation wiring

Hi Sophie / BrightBridge ops team —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Per our discussion I wanted to summarize a proposed 3-week kickstart to get Redwood telemetry and ops handoffs in place for your prod and staging environments. High level deliverables we plan to deliver in that window: 

- Baseline dashboard set (latency P50/P95, token throughput, error rates, model fallbacks)
- Tracing hooks and span names for request <-> model mapping and tool calls
- Error taxonomy document (client errors, model errors, infra errors)
- Alert routing matrix + on-call playbook (who gets paged for what)
- Runbook template with escalation steps and postmortem checklist

Proposed kickoff & sprint cadence:
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, access, sample data exchange, confirm dashboards
- Week 1: implement tracing hooks + sample dashboards in staging
- Week 2: validate alerts + runbook walkthrough; production cutover plan

Questions / constraints I noted from today's call: 1) retention/pseudonymization requirements for traces; 2) who the on-call recipient is for model regressions; 3) whether BrightBridge wants RBAC for dashboard edit vs view.

I've attached a lightweight kickstart-checklist.xlsx and a sample-dashboard.json that we can iterate on. Can you confirm the following by EOD Wednesday so we can lock the sprint:

1) Which Slack channel should alerts post to (ops or infra)?
2) Person to be on primary on-call for model regressions (name + email)
3) Any internal compliance constraints for trace retention > 30 days

Thanks — I can schedule a 30-min kickoff tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Onboarding Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
attachments: kickstart-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats), sample-dashboard.json (application/json)
From: Sophie Tran <sophie@brightbridge.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Apr 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability kickstart: dashboards, tracing hooks & escalation wiring

Hi Mateo —

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers from our side:

- Send alerts to #bb-ops-alerts (we'll also mirror to #bb-incident)
- Primary on-call for model regressions: Daniel Park (daniel.park@brightbridge.ai)
- Retention: logs and traces can be retained up to 90 days internal, but anything with PII must be redacted. We will not allow storing raw prompts beyond 30 days.

We have an internal doc that lists our on-call rotations; I'll share after the kickoff. Kickoff tomorrow at 10am PT works for us.

Two asks from our SRE side: 
1) Can Redwood provide an opt-in masking layer for traces that strips prompt text?
2) We prefer alerting with both Slack and PagerDuty for Sev2+.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Tran
Ops Lead, BrightBridge

Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Tran <sophie@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Apr 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability kickstart: dashboards, tracing hooks & escalation wiring

Folks —

Quick technical notes after an initial review of the sample-dashboard.json and the BrightBridge constraints: 

- Masking: we can support prompt masking at ingestion with two levels: (A) full prompt redaction, (B) token-level hash with reversible keys (KMS-managed). Option A is immediate but loses prompt text for debugging; Option B requires a short integration window for key exchange.
- Tracing: we'll supply span names as redwood.request, redwood.model_call, redwood.tool_call and attach a lightweight trace attribute model_id and request_id. We'll avoid including raw prompt fields by default; opt-in attachment possible.
- Alerts: suggest Slack for P1/P2, PagerDuty for P1/P2 on-call escalation. We'll provide a JSON alert routing matrix with conditions (error_rate > 0.5% over 5m, model_fallback_count > 3 in 10m, latency.p95 > 3s).

I'll prototype the masking toggle and drop a short proof-of-concept by Thu EOD. Laura — can you prepare the dashboard view with the model_fallback panel and an alert example?

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: none
From: ops@brightbridge.ai <ops@brightbridge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Apr 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability kickstart: dashboards, tracing hooks & escalation wiring

Marissa / Mateo / Ben —

Thanks for the updates and the clear list of options. Daniel (cc'd on his personal line below) will own the on-call side and can work with Ben on the PagerDuty mapping. For masking, BrightBridge prefers Option B (token-level hash with KMS), but we can pilot Option A for staging if Option B will take longer than two weeks.

Two clarifications from our security team: 
- If you use KMS-managed reversible keys, we'll need a short security review and an HMAC log of key rotations.
- We require the runbook to include an incident privacy checklist (steps to redact user prompts before any external comms).

We'll be ready for the kickoff tomorrow 10am PT. Looking forward to the runbook-template.md and the initial dashboard by Friday.

Regards,
BrightBridge Ops
